expectations_used.clarify: Reads the failing test output and the failing test body before editing source; asks about intended behavior where the spec is ambiguous.
expectations_used.approach: States a hypothesis about the MECHANISM of the failure (what the code does wrong, not merely which file) before changing code.
expectations_used.communicate: Narrates the investigation: what the failure says, what is suspected, what each change is meant to prove.
expectations_used.implement: Makes targeted changes that test the stated hypothesis; instruments (prints/reads state) rather than guessing when stuck.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs the suite after the fix and confirms the previously-failing test passes and nothing else broke.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains the root cause and why the fix addresses it.

summary: The candidate ran the tests once, gave only a vague and incomplete reading of the failure when pressed by the interviewer, opened two files that were not the location of the actual bug, and then ended the session after a long silent stretch without making any code changes or reaching a fix.

dimensions.analysis: When prompted by the interviewer to explain the failure before diving in, the candidate only vaguely referenced a deep-equal mismatch without identifying which fields differed or what the test scenario actually was (multiple holds expiring in one sweep). No question was asked to resolve ambiguity, and the actual failure diff was never articulated in specifics.

The candidate never stated a hypothesis about a mechanism; they opened src/shipments.ts and src/types.ts, which are not the files containing the actual defect (src/holdStore.ts), suggesting a guess based on the word 'shipment' rather than a reasoned theory about what the code does wrong.

After the interviewer's prompt, the candidate gave only fragmentary, hedging remarks about deep equality without narrating any concrete plan or reasoning chain, and then went silent for nearly 3 minutes while files were open with no further speech captured.
No code edits are recorded in the timeline; the candidate only opened two files and then ended the session without making any changes.
No fix was implemented, so there was nothing to verify; the suite was only run once at the very start before any investigation.
The session ended with the candidate clicking End Session without any resolution, explanation of root cause, or summary of findings.
